description: How persisted EvalResults roll up into the four product areas of the HAR-145 Ghost Eval Control Plane. An EvalResult's eval_type belongs to exactly one registry family (contracts/evals/eval_registry.json, E1-E22), and each family to exactly one area. HAR-145 puts the whole decision and feedback loop under Decision & Learning, decision construction and ranking, the human interaction, edit propagation, action generation, tool use, execution, knowledge mutation and its later use, so E5-E17 are all there. The three buckets and their gates (eval_registry.json) organise the evals inside the areas; they do not replace them. Cliff / Experience holds the messages and no eval family; System is operational only (E18-E22). The operational diagnostics M1-M5 are metrics, never evals, and belong to no area (they are served as OperationalMetrics). family_spans says which TraceSpan kind (episode_trace.v1.json) an EvalResult of a family is attached to by default; an eval whose span differs says so in the registry (`span_kind`). The validation and safety families E18-E22 have no span and are listed on the trace as unassigned. grounding and timing_cadence are each split by what they judge: decision_grounding / decision_timing (E8: the strategy) and artifact_grounding / artifact_timing (E12: the action artifact), so no judge serves two evals; the two older names remain until the split judges ship and each serves one eval. core-go/internal/evalarea mirrors this file; a parity test keeps them identical.

source.note: The registry links E-evals to catalog types many-to-many and leaves 13 catalog types unlinked; this file picks the one primary family per type, and a test checks it is one of the registry's own links where the registry has any.
